html:
Skip to main content

Step 1 of 3

Every ZIP code in the country, from federal data

Nothing here is stored on a server, and this site holds no copy of the data. Your browser fetches every figure directly from its publisher, so any number on screen can be checked against the original source by anyone.

Look up a single ZIP code above and it works immediately, with no account. To load all 33,791 at once, the Census Bureau asks for a free API key so they can track usage.

Every ZIP code in the country, from federal data. Step 1 of 3.

CivicScope

Every ZIP code in the US, from federal data, in your browser.

Ask CivicScope

Free-text Ask sends the words you type to the wording helper; this path cannot be answered from structured choices alone. The figures still come from CivicScope.

Figures are CivicScope's (source and vintage shown with each figure). Wording is Muse Spark's. This is a reading of the shown figures, not an additional source.

Look up a ZIP code or a city

Search by five-digit US ZIP code, or by city and state. City suggestions come from the Census Bureau and list every ZIP code in the matched city.

A five-digit ZIP code goes straight to that area. A city name offers every ZIP code inside it, so you can pick the neighbourhood rather than whichever one comes first.

A free Census key is needed to load the data.

Unlock the full housing and demographic dataset

The Census Bureau requires every app to hold a free API key so they can track usage. It takes about a minute, and your key is stored only in this browser — it is never sent to us, and we keep no log of what you search for.

  1. Open the free Census key form in a new tab.
  2. Fill in three fields. You can leave the organisation as “Individual”.
  3. The key arrives by email. Paste it below.

About school data here: district staffing and enrollment figures cover all 50 states. Near this location, the national source can show up to eight nearest public schools within 3 km with a reportable 2019 four-year graduation-rate midpoint; many records instead contain a published range, and missing or suppressed outcomes are omitted. NYC’s separate DOE directory still supplies named-school enrollment, graduation and attendance figures from 2018–19. Neither source is a school-quality rating.

Saved comparisons

Kept in this browser only. A saved comparison is a set of ZIP codes and nothing else — never an ordering or a filter.

Nothing saved yet. Select some areas above, then name the comparison to keep it.

This tool is free, and stays free

CivicScope carries no advertising, sells no listings, and takes no payment for placement in any result. It runs on free hosting and free government data, so there is nothing for a sponsor to buy.

If it saved you time or answered a question you could not otherwise afford to answer, you can chip in towards hosting. These are voluntary gifts to the person who maintains it.

  • PayPal
  • Venmo - @lucas-ballek
  • Cash App - $luball

Contributions are voluntary gifts to an individual, not payment for a service, and are not tax-deductible. They buy nothing: no priority support, no guarantees, and no promise about future features. No contribution can change any figure, ranking or result on this site.

These links go to personal accounts, not to a public collective, so the balance is not published and the funds are the maintainer’s. That is a weaker guarantee than a collective would give, and it is stated here rather than implied away — see docs/governance.md for the full position.

How to read this data

  • Every figure here describes a Census-defined area — a ZIP code tabulation area or census tract. It does not describe any individual, household, property, or its occupants.
  • These are survey estimates with margins of error. Small areas are less reliable than large ones, and each figure shows its own uncertainty.
  • We show public statistical data and where it came from. The national list starts in ZIP code order; readers may sort it by one figure. That is not an overall ranking or a recommendation. We do not endorse neighborhoods or sell, broker, or refer listings. The selected-area view includes a limited affordability index with its inputs and weights; Similar ZIP search is optional and lists matches alphabetically. This tool is not legal advice.
  • The federal Fair Housing Act prohibits housing discrimination based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex, disability, and familial status. State and local protections may also apply.

Equal Housing Opportunity

If you believe you have experienced housing discrimination, you can contact HUD, a HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program partner, or the Department of Justice:

  • U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development
  • HUD Fair Housing Assistance Program state and local agencies
  • U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division
  • National Fair Housing Alliance

HUD’s directory lists participating agencies. It is a starting point for local help, not a complete statement of the law in any state or city.

CivicScope is free, open, and carries no advertising. It does not sell, broker, or refer listings and does not accept payment for placement in any result.

Data is fetched directly from its publishers by your browser. We operate no server that records your searches, and we hold no copy of the data.

This product uses the Census Bureau Data API but is not endorsed or certified by the Census Bureau. Geocoding by OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
